active_paradigms.idea: Direct min-max bisection feasibility with per-GPU load bounds
active_paradigms.description: Binary search on target KVPR T. For a given T, each GPU g with size S must satisfy W_g/(M-S_g) <= T, i.e., W_g + T*S_g <= T*M. This is a generalized assignment problem: assign each model j with weight v_j and size s_j to a GPU such that sum(v_j + T*s_j) <= T*M per GPU. Use a greedy/branch-and-bound feasibility check (or LP relaxation with linprog to verify feasibility bound). Binary search T to high precision and construct the final placement from the feasible assignment at the best T. This directly optimizes the true objective rather than hill climbing.
active_paradigms.cautions: Feasibility check must be robust; fall back to current hill climb if infeasible. Handle empty GPUs (S=0 gives KVPR 0).

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing on move/swap neighborhood with temperature schedule
active_paradigms.description: Replace deterministic hill climbing (which gets stuck in local optima) with simulated annealing using the same move/swap neighborhood. Accept worsening moves with probability exp(-delta/T), cool T geometrically. Score is max KVPR with sum KVPR as tiebreaker. Run multiple annealing restarts from different greedy initializations within the time budget. Pure Python, no extra libraries needed.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via escaping local optima
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep iteration count within eval timeout; cache W/S per GPU for O(1) delta evaluation; ensure memory constraint checked before every move.

active_paradigms.idea: LPT-style balanced partitioning on effective load including capacity slack
active_paradigms.description: Reframe each model's effective load as v_j + T*s_j for an estimated target T (start with total load/(total capacity)). Sort models by effective load descending and assign each to the GPU that minimizes resulting max KVPR while fitting memory (best-fit on the combined metric), iterating T until consistent. This gives a much better starting point than plain v_j ordering, then apply the existing repair loop. Key insight: models with large size consume KVPR denominator, so size must factor into ordering.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: initial placement quality feeding into local search, primary score
active_paradigms.cautions: Handle models that fit only on empty GPUs (size near M); iterate T only a few times to stay fast.

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary search on target KVPR with feasibility check via bin packing
tried_paradigms.description: The objective is minimize max over GPUs of W_g/(M - S_g) where W_g = sum r_j/s_j, S_g = sum sizes. Fix a threshold T; a GPU is feasible under T if placing a set of models keeps W_g <= T*(M - S_g). Binary search on T and check feasibility by packing models into at most gpu_num GPUs using a greedy/first-fit on the linearized constraint (each model j consumes size s_j and weight w_j; GPU capacity pair (mem, T*(M-S_g))). Use first-fit-decreasing on w_j/s_j ratio with the feasibility test 'W_g + w_j <= T*(M - (S_g + s_j))'. Binary search ~40 iterations gives near-optimal max KVPR.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score (minimize max KVPR across GPUs)
tried_paradigms.cautions: Handle models that alone exceed feasibility (must still place them; use max over single-model GPUs as lower bound). Ensure exact-fit memory edge cases (denominator zero) treated carefully; keep T range [min single-model KVPR, sum all weights / small epsilon].
tried_paradigms.approach_type: custom binary search + first-fit bin packing

tried_paradigms.idea: Local search: greedy initial placement followed by swap/move hill climbing on max KVPR
tried_paradigms.description: Start from the current greedy placement. Then iteratively improve: repeatedly find the GPU with maximum KVPR, and try moving one of its models to another GPU or swapping a model with a model from another GPU; accept any move that reduces the max KVPR (or lexicographically reduces the sorted KVPR vector). Continue until no improving move exists or an iteration cap (e.g., 500) is reached. Tie-break by second-highest KVPR to enable cascading improvements.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score; also reduces second-highest KVPR for robustness
tried_paradigms.cautions: Always check memory feasibility before a move; keep O(n^2) move evaluation cheap by caching per-GPU W and S sums. Deterministic tie-breaking to avoid infinite loops.

tried_paradigms.idea: Balanced partitioning via LPT-style scheduling on weight-per-memory with capacity-aware assignment using linear_sum_assignment
tried_paradigms.description: Formulate as: compute per-model value v_j = r_j/s_j and size s_j. Aim to equalize the ratio across GPUs. Use scipy.optimize.linprog relaxation: variables x_{gj} in [0,1], constraints sum_g x_{gj}=1, sum_j s_j x_{gj} <= M - epsilon, minimize T s.t. sum_j (r_j/s_j) x_{gj} <= T*(M - sum_j s_j x_{gj}) for all g. Solve LP, then round fractional assignments greedily (assign each model to its highest-fraction GPU if memory allows, else best-fit), and finish with a repair pass.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via LP lower bound + rounding
tried_paradigms.cautions: LP size is gpu_num*n_models; fine for small test cases. The rounding step must guarantee all models placed; fall back to best-fit for unplaced models. Use small epsilon memory slack to avoid zero denominators.

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary search on target KVPR threshold T with linearized feasibility assignment (Dinkelbach-style)
tried_paradigms.description: The core difficulty is the ratio objective max_g W_g/(M-S_g). Convert it to a sequence of linear feasibility problems: for a candidate threshold T, GPU g is feasible iff sum(r_i) <= T*(M - sum(s_i)) for assigned models, i.e., sum(r_i + T*s_i) <= T*M. Binary search T over [0, upper]. For each T, run a first-fit-decreasing assignment where each model j is placed on a GPU minimizing remaining slack of the linearized load (r_j + T*s_j), models sorted by r_j + T*s_j descending. If all models fit, lower T; else raise. This directly attacks the true objective instead of hill-climbing on a compound (max, sum) score. Use ~30 binary search iterations with greedy restarts per T (a few random orderings).
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score (min max KVPR) directly, avoiding local optima of hill climbing
tried_paradigms.cautions: Feasibility is not monotone in T for a fixed greedy order, so use multiple orderings per T to reduce noise; keep the best feasible placement found across all T; guard against infeasibility (return greedy fallback).
tried_paradigms.approach_type: custom binary search + greedy first-fit (no external optimizer)

tried_paradigms.idea: LP relaxation via scipy.optimize.linprog for lower bound plus randomized rounding repair
tried_paradigms.description: Relax the assignment to fractional: variables x[j][g] in [0,1], constraints sum_g x[j][g] = 1 and per-GPU sum_j r_j*x[j][g] - T*s_j*x[j][g] <= 0 for a guessed T. Solve with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) to find a fractional assignment minimizing T (or feasibility at fixed T via binary search). Then round: sort fractional assignments and assign each model to its highest-x GPU if memory allows, otherwise the GPU with best KVPR impact; finish with the existing swap/move local search as a repair step. The LP gives a strong lower bound and a globally informed starting point, escaping the greedy's structural bias.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: closeness to the true optimum of max KVPR; global structure of the assignment
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep LP small (models x GPUs variables); if linprog fails or is slow, fall back to greedy; ensure memory constraint S_g < M is enforced during rounding; use HiGHS method explicitly.

tried_paradigms.idea: Targeted simulated annealing focused on the bottleneck GPU with ejection-chain moves
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the exhaustive pairwise best-improvement hill climb (which is O(n^2) per step and gets stuck) with simulated annealing that concentrates moves on the argmax-KVPR GPU: repeatedly pick the worst GPU, try moving one of its models to any other GPU, or swapping with a model on another GPU, accepting equal/worse moves with temperature-based probability. Add ejection chains: move model out of worst GPU, and if the receiving GPU becomes the new bottleneck, cascade a move from it. Use geometric cooling from a temperature scaled by the current max KVPR. Multiple short annealing runs from the greedy start, keeping the best.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: escape local optima of the (max, sum) compound score; specifically reduce the bottleneck GPU's KVPR
tried_paradigms.cautions: Always maintain W/S caches and feasibility (S < M); cap iterations for runtime; use a deterministic seed for reproducibility; keep the greedy+repair result as fallback if annealing never improves.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: custom simulated annealing with ejection chains
